'''Harald August Bohr''' (22 April 1887 – 22 January 1951) was a [[Denmark|Danish]] [[mathematician]] and [[Football player|footballer]]. After receiving his doctorate in 1910, Bohr became an eminent mathematician, founding the field of [[almost periodic function]]s. His brother was the [[Nobel Prize]]-winning physicist [[Niels Bohr]]. He was on the [[Denmark national football team|Denmark national team]] for the [[1908 Summer Olympics]], where he won a silver medal.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.olympedia.org/athletes/24628 |title=Harald Bohr |work=Olympedia |access-date=26 March 2021}}</ref>

==Biography==
Bohr was born in 1887 to [[Christian Bohr]], a professor of physiology, from a Lutheran background, and Ellen Adler Bohr, a woman from a wealthy Jewish family of local renown.<ref name="StAbio">{{cite web
|url=http://www-history.mcs.st-andrews.ac.uk/Biographies/Bohr_Harald.html
|title=Harald August Bohr
|access-date=2008-08-17
|author=J J O'Connor and E F Robertson}}</ref> Harald had a close relationship with his elder brother, which ''[[The Times]]'' likened to that between Captain Cuttle and Captain Bunsby in [[Charles Dickens]]' ''[[Dombey and Son]]''.<ref>{{cite news
|title=Obituary: Prof. Harald Bohr |work=[[The Times]] |page=8 |date=6 February 1951 |via=Times Digital Archive 1785–1985}}</ref>

==Mathematical career==
Like his father and brother before him, in 1904 Bohr enrolled at the [[University of Copenhagen]], where he studied mathematics, obtaining his master's degree in 1909 and his doctorate a year later. Among his tutors were [[Hieronymus Georg Zeuthen]] and [[Thorvald N. Thiele]].<ref name="BullAm">{{cite journal |last=Bochner |first=Salomon |author-link=Salomon Bochner |date=January 1952 |title=Harald Bohr |journal=Bulletin of the American Mathematical Society |volume=58 |issue=1 |pages=72–75 |url=http://projecteuclid.org/DPubS/Repository/1.0/Disseminate?handle=euclid.bams/1183516518&view=body&content-type=pdf_1 |access-date=2008-12-21 |doi=10.1090/S0002-9904-1952-09551-3 |doi-access=free }}</ref> Bohr worked in mathematical analysis; much of his early work was devoted to [[Dirichlet series]] including his doctorate, which was entitled ''Bidrag til de Dirichletske Rækkers Theori'' (''Contributions to the Theory of Dirichlet Series'').<ref name="Boas">
{{cite arXiv
|eprint=math.CV/9705204
|title=The Football Player and the Infinite Series
|author=H. P. Boas
|year=1997
}}</ref> A collaboration with [[Göttingen]]-based [[Edmund Landau]] resulted in the [[Bohr–Landau theorem]], regarding the distribution of zeroes in [[Riemann zeta function|zeta function]]s.<ref name="StAbio"/>

Bohr worked in [[mathematical analysis]], founding the field of [[almost periodic function]]s, and worked with the [[University of Cambridge|Cambridge]] mathematician [[G. H. Hardy]].

In 1915, he became a professor at [[Polyteknisk Læreanstalt]] (today [[Technical University of Denmark]]), working there until 1930, when he took a professorship at the University of Copenhagen. He remained in this post for 21 years until his death in 1951. [[Børge Jessen]] was one of his students there.

He was a visiting professor at [[Stanford University]] during the academic year 1930–1931.<ref>{{cite journal|author=Putnam, T. M.|title=The November meeting in Los Angeles|journal=Bull. Amer. Math. Soc.|volume=37|year=1931|pages=3–5|doi=10.1090/S0002-9904-1931-05068-0|doi-access=free}}</ref> He was a visiting scholar at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] in the summer of 1948.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ias.edu/scholars|title=Scholars|website=Institute for Advanced Study|date=14 August 2015}}</ref>

Bohr was known as a good teacher, and the annual award for outstanding teaching at the [[University of Copenhagen]] is called the Harald, in honour of Harald Bohr.{{Citation needed|date=March 2026}} With [[Johannes Mollerup]], Bohr wrote an influential four-volume textbook ''Lærebog i Matematisk Analyse'' (''Textbook in mathematical analysis'').<ref>{{cite web |title=Bibliography of Harald Bohr |url=http://www.math.ku.dk/ths/bohr_h/biblio.htm |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090728063139/http://www.math.ku.dk/ths/bohr_h/biblio.htm |archive-date=28 July 2009 |access-date=2008-08-20 |publisher=University of Copenhagen}}</ref>

Bohr was elected to the [[American Philosophical Society]] in 1945.<ref>{{Cite web |title=APS Member History |url=https://search.amphilsoc.org/memhist/search?creator=Harald+Bohr&title=&subject=&subdiv=&mem=&year=&year-max=&dead=&keyword=&smode=advanced |access-date=2023-03-31 |website=search.amphilsoc.org}}</ref>

In the 1930s Bohr was a leading critic of the anti-Semitic policies taking root in the German mathematical establishment, publishing an article criticising [[Ludwig Bieberbach]]'s ideas in ''[[Weekendavisen|Berlingske Aften]]'' in 1934.<ref>{{cite book |last=Menzler-Trott |first=Eckart |title=Logic's Lost Genius: The Life of Gerhard Gentzen |publisher=AMS |year=2008 |isbn=978-0-8218-3550-0| page=115}}</ref> Following the murder of [[Kaj Munk]] on 4 January 1944 the Danish resistance newspaper ''[[De frie Danske]]'' brought condemning reactions from influential Scandinavians, including Bohr.<ref>{{cite news |date=January 1944 |title=KAJ MUNK IN MEMORIAM |url=http://www.illegalpresse.dk/papers#/paper?paper=68&page=685 |access-date=18 November 2014 |newspaper=[[De frie Danske]] |page=6 |language=da |quote=Meddelelsen om denne nye Voldsdaad i Danmark, Mordet paa en af vore største Digtere og modigste Personligheder, har opfyldt os alle med Afsky og Forfærdelse, og vi forstaar, at Kaj Munks Anseelse og den Beundring man nærede for ham her i Sverige, var saa stor, at vore Følelser deles af det svenske Folk}}</ref>

==Football==
[[File:DK football1908.jpg|thumb|Danish football team at the [[Football at the 1908 Summer Olympics|1908 Olympic games]]. Bohr is in the top row, 2nd from left.]]
Bohr was also an excellent football player. He had a long playing career with [[Akademisk Boldklub]], making his debut as a 16-year-old in 1903.<ref name="AB">{{cite web|url=http://www.ab-fodbold.dk/ab-as.aspx |title=AB's historie |access-date=2008-08-18 |author=Akademisk Boldklub |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081210175841/http://ab-fodbold.dk/ab-as.aspx |archive-date=10 December 2008 }}</ref> During the 1905 season he played alongside his brother [[Niels Bohr|Niels]], who was a goalkeeper. Harald was selected to play for the [[Denmark national football team|Denmark national team]] in the [[1908 Summer Olympics]], where football was an official event for the first time. Though a Danish side had played at the [[Football at the 1906 Intercalated Games|1906 Intercalated Games]], the opening match of the 1908 Olympic tournament was Denmark's first official international football match. Bohr scored two goals as Denmark beat the French "B" team 9–0.<ref name="sportsref1">{{cite web
|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/athletes/bo/harald-bohr-1.html
|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200418093508/https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/athletes/bo/harald-bohr-1.html
|url-status=dead
|archive-date=2020-04-18
|title=Harald Bohr
|access-date=2008-08-18
|publisher=Sports-Reference.com}}</ref> In the next match, the semi-final, Bohr played in a 17–1 win against [[France national football team|France]], which remains an Olympic record.<ref name="sportsref2">{{cite web
|url=http://results.beijing2008.cn/WRM/ENG/BCK/FB/36192.shtml
|title=Facts and figures – Team achievements / records
|access-date=2008-08-18
|publisher=Beijing Olympics 2008 official website|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080905231854/http://results.beijing2008.cn/WRM/ENG/BCK/FB/36192.shtml|archive-date=2008-09-05}}</ref> Denmark faced hosts [[Great Britain men's Olympic football team|Great Britain]] in the final, but lost 2–0, and Bohr won a silver medal.<ref name="StAbio"/><ref name="Boas"/> After the Olympics he made one further appearance for the national team, in a 2–1 victory against an England amateur team in 1910.<ref name="RSSSF1">{{cite web
|url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablesd/den-intl0812.html
|title=Denmark – Internationals 1908–1912
|access-date=2008-08-18
|publisher=Rec.Sport.Soccer Statistics Foundation}}</ref> His popularity as a footballer was such that when he defended his doctoral thesis the audience was reported as having more football fans than mathematicians.<ref name="plus">{{cite web
|url=http://plus.maths.org/blog/2007/01/mathematical-moments-harald-bohr.html
|title=Mathematical Moments – Harald Bohr
|date=23 January 2007
|access-date=2008-08-20
|publisher=Plus magazine
|archive-date=17 May 2008
|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080517050954/http://plus.maths.org/blog/2007/01/mathematical-moments-harald-bohr.html
|url-status=dead
}}</ref>
